newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX power ends up on shortcovering, steady cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX power ends up on shortcovering, steady cash.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled higher Thursday in light volume amid short-covering and steady cash prices in the western physical power prices.
"There are people who are still worried being short for the summer," a Houston marketer said when asked about the reason that underpinned today's rise.
August Palo Verde (PV) futures settled up 79 cents at $35.49 a megawatt hour (MWh) after posting a high at $35.75.
September PV finished up 97 cents at $28.70. October PV, the other active contract, ended up 60 cents at $23.00.
August California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled up nine cents at $21.10 a MWh, trimming a 49 cent gain.
September COB finished up 58 cents at $22.08. Other COB months ended five to 14 cents higher.

The complex seemed to extend Wednesday's rise on news that the 1,221 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Palo Verde nuclear complex near Phoenix, Arizona would begin Sunday to slowly ramp down to between 60 and 80 percent power by September 6, when it was scheduled to shut for refueling.
There was plenty of supply in the West, with units ramping up and more power flowing on the Pacific Intertie, to make up for the coastdown at Palo Verde 2, market sources said.
A 700 unit at the Colstrip coal-fired power plant in Montana was said to restart today after being shut last Friday for unplanned repairs.

The 1,070 MW unit 2 at San Onofre nuclear power station in southern California reached 98 percent power early Thursday, while the neighboring 1,080 MW unit 3 was at 86 percent and was increasing to full power.

On Wednesday, the Western Systems Coordinating Council approved a final summertime capacity for the Pacific Intertie of 6,900 megawatts (MW). The new rating will replace an interim summer cap of 6,300 MW which took effect July 1.
Some players perceived August futures to be overpriced due to rising supply availability in the Southwest.
"Cash and futures are ridiculously high," a Houston futures trader said.
Firm, peak power prices at PV firmed to $28.50-31.50 from Wednesday's $27.50-28.50. and those at COB eased to $16.75-17.75 from $17.00-18.00 yesterday.
Brokers and traders were uncertain about the direction of the complex ahead of expiration of August options tomorrow and August futures Monday.
To narrow to their sharp differential, cash prices need to rise to meet futures or futures must to fall to converge with cash, they said.
"It's going to be interesting which one is going to do it cash or futures," another Houston trader said.

Forecasts called for temperatures in the Pacific Northwest to be coolest over the central and eastern areas over the next week, averaging three to five degrees Fahrenheit below normal, with readings one to two degrees below normal in the west.

In the Southwest, temperatures were expected to average three to five degrees below normal over most of the region through into early next week, with temperatures near normal in the extreme east, south and west sections.
((--R Leong, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1622))
